The header (rows 1-8) is a front-facing strip: crimson rows 1-2 are the same lightness (L=59) as row 6, so there is no distinct top plane, and the white label in rows 3-5 is a vertical panel. Rows 7-9 are dark outline or shadow, not a separate top surface. The base (rows 30-31) is a 2-row gray strip. The silhouette widths (12, 14, 16, then 14) show no widening and narrowing that would make an ellipse. This is a flat front elevation with no readable top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a red vertical sign with a dark red-brown outline that leans toward the material, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so it does not have the near-black sticker outline. The cap, body, cream text panel and lettering are separated by value, and the body shows a lit side and a shaded side. It has 7 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for bus-shelter-a. It has only 8 distinct colours in total, so its ramps are about 4 steps against 5-6 in the richer references, and its density is slightly below the median of the references. It is a thin single-tile prop, though, and is no flatter or more sticker-like than the accepted bus-shelter-a, so a careful artist would accept it beside the references.
